Packing tips

Packing and labelling your boxes

Good labelling saves hours on arrival. The simple method so every box goes straight to the right room.

4 min read · Updated 14 October 2026

Contents

  1. One box, one room
  2. What to write
  3. Colour coding
  4. The list that goes with it
  5. Spreading the weight
  6. FAQ

Need tailored advice?

Boxes & supplies

One box, one room

Pack room by room and do not mix contents. A “kitchen” box should only hold kitchen items: it will go straight into the kitchen, and you will know where to look.

What to write

  • The destination room, in the new home.
  • A box number.
  • The contents in a few words.
  • “FRAGILE” and “this way up” if needed.

Write on two sides and on top: the box stays readable even when stacked.

Colour coding

Give each room a colour: a coloured label or tape on every box, and the same colour stuck on the room’s door on arrival. Movers put boxes in the right place without asking you.

The list that goes with it

Keep a simple list: number, room, contents. On your phone, a photo of the contents before closing the box is enough. If in doubt on arrival, you find everything in seconds.

Spreading the weight

  • Heavy items at the bottom, light ones on top.
  • Boxes you can lift easily.
  • Boxes to open first marked “PRIORITY”.

Cody’s tip

Stick a simple plan of the new home by the entrance, with the room colours: the whole team finds its way at a glance.

Frequently asked questions

Should boxes be numbered?

It is very useful: with a list, you check on arrival that every box is there, and quickly find what you need.

What goes in the priority box?

Essentials for the first days: chargers, papers, sheets, toiletries, a saucepan, coffee-making kit.
